## 1. PyCQA/isort #2781: Keep the grouping of commented `from` imports stable across runs
- Repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/isort
- PR: https://github.com/PyCQA/isort/pull/2781 by PDGGK, last updated 2026-11-03 15:41 IST (2026-11-03T10:11:41Z), mergeable_state unstable (CI), 1 commit
- Head: 3936b83f05317a8049a572fcf192a98bbb9d4be1
- Base: 841e43126cd2ca74751b421afd00d90ca36932e5 (main; = merge base, 1 ahead, 0 behind)
- Claims: on main (from the grouping added in #2614), `from` imports carrying comments that can't share one statement are not idempotent: a second isort run regroups them and moves comments onto other names (e.g. `# noqa: F401` ends up covering `basename, dirname, exists, join`), so `isort --check` fails on just-sorted output. Fix: only the first statement for a module may group commented names or move a `noqa` to its opening line; the grouping loop now skips (continue) instead of stopping (break) at a name whose comment can't join. Changes isort/output.py (30+/13-) and adds regression tests in tests/unit/test_regressions.py.
- Expected verdict: **verified.** Probe the PR's own example (`from os.path import basename  # used below` / `dirname` / `exists  # noqa: F401` / `join`): first-run output differs between base and head (claimed), and on head running isort twice gives the same text and `--check` passes, while base changes on the second run.
- Watch: the first-run output change is part of the claim (the break-to-continue change regroups names after a commented one), so differences on commented `from` imports are claimed, not unclaimed. Uncommented imports must be identical both sides. Idempotency needs a two-pass probe; a one-pass probe only sees "output differs".
- Setup: pure Python, no compile. Must be installed (version read from metadata): `SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION=x pip install --no-deps --force-reinstall .` per side; runtime dep mypy-extensions. `hypothesis` sits in the `dev` dependency group (fix 85), so skip tests/unit/test_parse.py and test_hypothesmith.py or install hypothesis. Subset: `pytest tests/unit/test_regressions.py -o addopts=""`; wider `pytest tests/unit --ignore=tests/unit/test_hypothesmith.py -o addopts=""`. All wheels pure. Install size: small.

## 2. mahmoud/boltons #732: Parse adjacent timedelta values without losing units
- Repo: https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons
- PR: https://github.com/mahmoud/boltons/pull/732 by Lushiyao5, last updated 2026-11-04 14:40 IST (2026-11-04T09:10:32Z), mergeable_state unstable, 1 commit
- Head: 7d74a6a63266a1d7b6d4da046482c5d0d41d5a5f
- Base: d31d821d56c8f7756af9c30a864077f2e5855321 (master; = merge base = master tip, 1 ahead, 0 behind)
- Claims: `timeutils.parse_timedelta` dropped units for adjacent values (`'1s2m'` gave 0:00:01, `'1h30m45.5s'` gave 1:00:00.5, `'1hour1minute'` gave 1:00:00). Now adjacent units add up, malformed numeric runs raise ValueError, full aliases (hour, minute, week...) keep working, and unsupported units such as `ms` are rejected. Changes boltons/timeutils.py (15+/3-), tests in tests/test_timeutils.py.
- Expected verdict: **verified.** Local probe (both files at exact SHAs): `'1s2m'` 0:00:01 base, 0:02:01 head; `'1h30m45.5s'` 1:00:00.5 vs 1:30:45.5; `'1hour1minute'` 1:00:00 vs 1:01:00; `'1h2'` 1:00:00 vs ValueError; `'1ms'` 0:01:00 (silently read as minutes) vs ValueError. Same both sides: `'1d 2h'`, `'1.5h'`, `'-1d'`, `'1 h'`, `'1s 2m'`, `'  3w '`, `''` (0:00:00), `'2 hours 3 minutes'`, and `'1x'` raises ValueError on both.
- Watch: the `'1ms'` change is claimed (the PR says ms is rejected), even though base actually accepted it silently. The ValueError message for a bad unit now lists all aliases instead of `w d h m s`; that is message text only and should be advisory at most.
- Setup: pure Python, no deps; `PYTHONPATH=.`. Subset: `pytest tests/test_timeutils.py -o addopts=""` (seconds). Install size: tiny.

## 3. encode/httpx #3741: Fix no_proxy to support IPV6 CIDR format
- Repo: https://github.com/encode/httpx
- PR: https://github.com/encode/httpx/pull/3741 by p3ck, last updated 2026-10-30 15:57 IST (2026-10-30T10:27:26Z), mergeable clean, 9 commits
- Head: 83d203a86d955b7695613df6378b56f9003112ce
- Base: b5addb64f0161ff6bfe94c124ef76f6a1fba5254 (master; = merge base = master tip, 9 ahead, 0 behind)
- Claims: `no_proxy=fe11::/16` made `httpx.Client()` fail (closes #3221). Now IPv6 CIDR entries become `all://[fe11::]/16` and a new `IPNetPattern` matches any address in the range; the docs say NO_PROXY now takes "hostnames/urls/ip ranges" and show `127.0.0.0/8` bypassing the proxy for 127.0.0.10. Changes httpx/_utils.py (74+/9-), httpx/_client.py (mount keys built with `build_url_pattern`), docs/environment_variables.md, tests/test_utils.py.
- Expected verdict: **verified.** Expected differences: `get_environment_proxies()` with `no_proxy=fe11::/16` gives `all://[fe11::/16]` on base and `all://[fe11::]/16` on head; `Client()` with that env fails on base and works on head; an IPv4 range mount (`all://192.168.0.0/24`) matches 192.168.0.1 on head but only the exact network address on base (base ignores the `/24` as a path).
- Watch, two false-alarm traps: (a) IPv4 range matching also changes (no_proxy `192.168.0.0/16` and user mounts like `all://10.0.0.0/8` now cover the whole range). Only the docs and tests state this, not the title, so a claim extractor that reads only the title will call it unclaimed. It is intended (docs example and new tests), so flagging it is a false alarm. (b) The private class `httpx._utils.URLPattern` is renamed to `WildcardURLPattern`, so base's tests/test_utils.py fails to import on head; that is a deleted/renamed private helper, the same pattern as click #3902 on 4 Nov, not a break. Range patterns also take priority over all wildcard mounts (priority -1); intended.
- Setup: pure Python (hatchling); `PYTHONPATH=.`. Do NOT install pytest-asyncio (filterwarnings=error gives INTERNALERROR). Subset: `pytest tests/test_utils.py -o addopts=""`; known env failures from 29 Oct (chardet decode, uvicorn logging) are in other files. Probes must set `no_proxy`/`NO_PROXY` and clear any sandbox proxy env vars. All wheels pure. Install size: small.
